guidelines: kansō is named after one of the seven principles of Zen art described by Shin'ichi Hisamatsu in Zen and the Fine Arts (1971). The design follows all seven as one philosophy, not taste.
Every guideline on these boards names the principle it serves. A decision that cannot name one is an opinion, and is not taken.
One limit sits above them: kansō removes information, never options. Every action stays one press away.

pages.page: Tokens/Kit: every value and every element, once
guidelines: Seijaku One kit. Every board and every mod uses these tokens and these pieces. A value outside the kit is a defect, and a piece drawn twice is a defect.

Fukinsei Hierarchy. Six roles, each with one size, weight and tone. Display 48 regular, the one number. Title 20 strong. Section 15 strong. Group 13.5 strong. Name 13.5 medium. Body 12.5 regular, with controls at 12.5 medium. Meta 11.5 regular in muted or dim. Size and weight tell the level; colour comes last.

Seijaku Space. Use the 4-based scale only: 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32. The same relation always gets the same gap. Icon to label is 8. Control to control is 8. Rows touch. Groups and fields are 12 apart. Panel padding is 16. Nothing is glued and nothing floats.

Seijaku Controls. Buttons and fields are 30 high, 12.5, with 12 inside. Buttons come in four kinds: solid (the one primary), tonal (a 7% foreground fill, no edge), quiet (text only) and armed. A field's label sits 8 above it, in 12.5 medium muted. A one-line state or a toast puts its action at the end of the line, 24 high with 8 inside. In a failure block the buttons start on the text column.

Shizen Live states. Washes come from the foreground: track 4%, hover 7%, selected 12%. Hover moves only tone, entering in 120 ms and leaving in 80 ms. Press uses the selected wash. Focus is a 2 px accent ring outside the box, on every control. Hover never reaches a disabled control and never replaces a state.
Kansō Armed. Only an action that cannot be undone asks twice. It fills with accent and reads "Press again to <verb>" for 4 s. Both labels share one cell, so nothing moves.
Seijaku States. Loading lives here. Failure, empty and pending live on S21, the one home for states.

Shizen Motion. Only three things move. The ensō spins at 900 ms. A working name shimmers with three glints over 2200 ms, with no dots. A blocked pane's bar breathes. Nothing changes size or place. Reduced motion holds everything still.
Kokō Icons. Use exact Lucide icons, one name per meaning, at 12, 14, 15 or 17. Show an icon only where it tells something apart. The ensō marks and program marks are marks, not icons.
Shizen Themes. Light and dark share the same geometry; only the tokens change. Text passes 4.5:1 and edges 3:1 in both themes. Light is never pure white.
Seijaku One drawing per state, everywhere, in the same words at every size. A view never invents its own.

Kansō Failure in the sidebar is a word on the row, as Off: the row keeps its icon and name, then the state in words (11.5 dim) and the fix as a row button at its end (Refresh, 20 with 12). No block grows under a row, so nothing moves and nothing shouts. The source's words, the fixes and Explain to <agent> live in the row's right-click menu, as its own actions (board 10).

Kansō Failure, block (panel): a 1 px blocked edge, no fill, radius 8, 12 inside. A 14 mark, then our words (13.5 medium, foreground), then the source's words as evidence (mono 11.5 muted, at most two lines; only when they are cut, the full text on hover, selectable, beside the block at the evidence's first line, never over the buttons). Buttons are 30 high and share the text column's width equally, 8 below it (where both do not fit on one line, each takes the full width): the fix first, solid (Refresh, or the write's own name), then Explain to <agent>, tonal, with the Lucide bot icon and the agent named in words, never a program mark, since any model can be behind it. No edges on these buttons. The row it belongs to does not repeat the state.
Kansō Where the block sits. Panel: where the list would start; a refused write, 2 under its row. In the sidebar a refused write is a toast, and the row returns to its state before the press.
Kansō Failure, line (toast, a one-line row): the mark, our words, and the fix at the end of the line, 24 high. A click on the line does the fix. No Explain at this size.
Fukinsei Failure in a bar (status bar 26, pane header 34): the mark, our words, and the fix right after them as a quiet button 20 high with no edge, so it keeps the bar's proportion.

Yūgen Empty: centred in the empty region, 24 above and below: the view's icon (20, dim), one sentence (12.5 muted, wraps balanced) and at most one tonal button. The action invites; it never shouts. No plate, no second sentence, no indent of its own.
Shizen Pending: the new state is drawn at once at 80% with a 4 px muted dot breathing beside it. Confirmed, both go. Refused, the old state returns with the failure block under it.
Kokō Colour: blocked only on the edge and the mark; words stay in foreground and muted. Contrast as in A.

This list is the only set. If you need another icon, take it from Lucide (lucide.dev/icons, version 1.72.0, ISC license). Copy its markup unchanged, add it here with an lu- id and the meaning it carries, and only then use it. One name per meaning, never a custom icon.
Every icon is Lucide 1.72.0, the icon's own markup, unchanged: 24 grid, stroke 2, round caps and joins. Ids are lu- and the Lucide name.
One name per meaning across every board: one close (lu-x), one more (lu-ellipsis), one pin, one sync, one share, one layers, one terminal.
A plain shell is lu-terminal, the same as the Terminal row in the + menu.
Not icons, kept: the ensō marks and spinner, the blocked mark, the Claude Code and Codex marks, Hachi's pixel art, the Dawn artwork, the kansō wordmark, the macOS window lights, the board pointer.
Flagged: Android has no Lucide icon (proposal: the word "Android" on the button). iOS uses lu-apple, the fruit, as the app does.
Seijaku Use a token, never a value. Every colour in a board or a mod is one of the tokens in the table. A new colour is added to the table, with its use and its rule, before anything uses it.
Shizen Text passes 4.5:1 on every surface it can sit on, including hover and selected. Marks, focus rings and control edges pass 3:1. Never lower contrast with opacity on text.
Fukinsei Three text levels: fg, muted and dim, told apart by size and place first and tone second.
Kokō One colour, one meaning. A state colour appears only on the thing in that state. Colour on anything that asks nothing is a defect.
Shizen Washes come from the foreground: track 4%, hover 7%, selected 12%, active project 14%. Light uses the same steps; it never reaches pure white or black.
Seijaku Light and dark are one design. They share the same geometry and the same token names; only the values differ.
Seijaku Checking a change. Any change to a token is measured against every surface in the table, hover and selected included, before it is published.
Fact | Its one home | Also shown, and why | Never shown in

An agent needs you | Its sidebar row: blocked wash, mark and the question (sidebar-agent). | Status bar, only while the row is out of view, as its stand-in. | Pane header and tab: no mark, no wash, no words; the pane shows the question itself. A dot on the view switch or the rail. A "Needs you" card.
What it asks | Its sidebar row's tooltip and its pane (sidebar-agent). | Status bar, only while the row is off screen, in the same words and the same cut. | A second, longer copy anywhere.
An agent finished, and its last words | Its pane. The row turns to the done mark until you look (sidebar-agent). | Nowhere else. | A digest on the done row.

What the turn changed: files, diff | Pane header segments (bars-header, bars-digest). | Nowhere else. A file's own stat in Files is a different fact. | A total in the Files panel. The same numbers on the sidebar row.
This agent is working | Its sidebar row: spinning ensō and name shimmer (sidebar-agent). | Nowhere else. | Pane header and tabs: no ensō. Edge dots.
How many agents are working | The spinning rows themselves (sidebar-agent); the Status view lists them. | Nowhere else. | A count on the status bar or the footer: it repeats the rows.
A command still running after the turn | The agent's row, by name ("pnpm dev") (sidebar-agent). | Nowhere else while Ports is closed. | A bare number.
The project's branch | Project row. A worktree's name is its branch (sidebar-project). | Nowhere else. | Pane header (folder and branch). Status bar.
Commits not pushed | Project row ↑N; a click opens Push (sidebar-project). | Nowhere else. | Pane header "N commits". Arrows that do nothing.
Behind upstream | Project row ↓N; a press pulls (sidebar-project). | Nowhere else. "Behind main" on a pull request is its base and lives in the header verdict. | Arrows that do nothing.
Pull request state | Pane header: #N and its verdict in words (bars-header). | Nowhere else at rest. The PR panel, when you open it, holds the detail. | A dot without words.
A check failed | The same pane header segment (bars-header). | Away card or toast, only when no header in view shows that PR. | The done row.
Reviews asked of me | PR list, first group, "Asked of you" (pr). | Status bar "2 reviews"; a click opens that group. | A count pill in the list.

A kansō update exists | The Settings menu in the footer, in words (sidebar-footer). | Toast, only while the footer is out of view, as its stand-in. | A dot on the gear or the footer. A banner in Settings.
Herdr has an update | The Settings menu, "Update Herdr" (sidebar-footer). | Nowhere else. | "Settings · update ready".
Which channel I am on | The sidebar header band, the pill, or nothing (dawn). | Nowhere else. | Toasts, the footer.
A computer's name | Its row at the head of its projects (sidebar-computer). | Nowhere else. | The status bar. A row for the only computer.

A computer stopped answering | Said once, when it happens: the away card, or a toast while you are here (sidebar-away). | Its actions stay one press away under + → Computers. | A standing "Unreachable" or "Off" on the list or the status bar.

Memory is low | Status bar, "Memory 8% free" (bars-status). | A system notice in the same words, only while no kansō window is on screen. | The status bar while the Memory panel is open: the panel holds it then.
A tab is asleep | The Asleep group; folded, its count is the summary (sidebar-asleep). | Nowhere else. | A second list in the Sleep dialog. A count beside the open rows.
Could not sleep | The asleep row: reason, Retry, Undo (sidebar-asleep). | Toast in the same words, only while the group is off screen. | The toast while the group is in view.
What happened while you were away | The away card: only facts no row in view shows (sidebar-away). | Nowhere else. | Needs you or Finished for a row in view. A count.
A server with no pane | Status bar ":6006 no pane"; a click opens Ports on that row (bars-status). | Nowhere else. | The status bar while Ports is open. A hero, a legend or a second line in Ports.

A container failed | Its row in Containers: "exited 1 · 3 min" (panels-b-containers). | Status bar "api-db exited 1", only while the panel is closed, as its stand-in. | Hero counts. "Docker is not installed".
Spend | The Spend panel, one number (panels-b-spend). | Nowhere else. | A dollar amount on the status bar. Crumbs, section counts, footnotes.
A file the agent named | Files, "Named by checkout" (panels-a-files). | Nowhere else. | A second listing under Also changed.
The command palette key | Settings · Keys, the one list of every key (dialogs-keys). | Nowhere else: you already know it. | The status bar. A second keyboard in Help.
Kansō One fact, one home. Every fact lives once, where it matters most. Less is more: no repeat, no second explanation, nothing you already know.

Yūgen A stand-in only while the home is out of view. The status bar or a toast may carry a fact only while its home is off screen or closed, and leaves when the home returns. Any other second place is a defect.
Kansō "Never shown in" lists places that must not carry the fact. A board or a build that puts it there is rejected.
Kansō Before adding anything visible, find its fact here. If it is new, add a row with its home before you draw it. If it already has a home elsewhere, do not draw it.
Kansō Facts you already know and cannot act on are not shown. They are said once, when they happen.

Kansō Every piece answers a right-click. Nothing is removed to keep the window quiet: a piece can be put away, and it comes back from the same place. Rest shows what you would miss. The rest stays one right-click away.

Seijaku One menu, one order. The title names the piece (Pull request · #166, PR panel). Next come the piece's own actions, then a rule. Last come the same three lines on every piece: Only when needed, Hide this, Settings for this…. Rows that already have a menu (agent, project, tab) keep their actions on top and end with these three.

Shizen Only when needed shows the piece only while it has something to say, such as a PR that is not ready or a check that failed. Hide this takes it off until you bring it back. Settings for this… opens Settings at that piece's switch, not at the top.

Kansō One press decides. Hide this acts at once with no confirmation. A toast in the corner names what left ("Hidden: Pull request") and what stops with it (gh stops for headers). Its one action is Undo, for 8 s.
Fukinsei Nothing moves around a hidden piece. Its neighbours close the gap on the same rhythm. They never jump or resize while the menu is open.
Kokō The menu is the kit's menu: the same rows, height, hover and rule as every other context menu. A terminal's own right-click stays the terminal's.
Yūgen Where to bring it back: right-click the region it lived in, or open Settings · Pieces, the one list of everything hidden.

Shizen Drawn from the app as it is (capture 2026-11-12, kanso-spaces/main.js, kanso-chrome/main.js, kanso-tabs/main.js, kanso-strip/main.js, kanso-status/main.js). Same regions, same controls, same places. Polish only: nothing new, nothing removed.

Seijaku One grid. A lead is 15 and its name follows 8 after, so each level steps 23: a machine's icon and a project's name at 8, its agents' icons under the machine's name at 31, a sub-agent's icon under its parent's name at 54. Rows are 32 (50 with a second line), groups 12 apart.

Seijaku One size per role, from K. Chrome (+, sort, search, hide, footer) 32 with 17. Bars (tabs, panels, pane tools) 26 with 15. Row buttons (+, power) 20 with 12; row tails (chevron, branch) 12; marks 14. Names 13.5, tabs and headers 12.5, secondary 11.5. Controls radius 6, panes 8.
Kokō Colour only for a state. ↓12 is a count, not a failure: muted, not red. Blocked lives on the mark (S21).

Shizen The user chooses what a row says. Right-click an agent (board 10): What it is on, Time in its state and Commands still running each take Show, Only when needed or Hide. At Only when needed, working and waiting sessions show a second line.

Kansō Title bar: the lights only. Herdr's mark and name leave. The footer: Update kansō while one is ready, then Settings, whose menu holds kansō settings, Herdr settings and Help. The tab bar's own gear and help go there; the account chip goes (its agent count was a second home).
Fukinsei The status bar is balanced: computer and branch at the left, the minimap in the middle, − 2 + at the right. Everything it shows stays.

Yūgen No fold chevron: the row itself folds. Open and at rest, a row is its name: you can see what it holds. Folded, it shows what it hides in its place: the most urgent mark and how many. The header shows the worktree by its last name (app-audit), the full path on hover, so the branch is never cut.

Fukinsei Nothing changes size. At rest a row is its lead, name and ensō. + and ⋯ appear on the row under the pointer in their own place; project and session row actions are not drawn at rest. Pane tools beyond sleep and send appear over the header's right end. A panel button shows its name only while its panel is open. No counting dots after a working name.
Yūgen Selection is one wash: the active project, the active tab and the focused pane header share it. No coloured outline.
Kansō Kept as it is: dark "Off" with its power button (you can act on it), the Update row, the tree lines, every panel button.
Shizen Two modes, named everywhere: Stable Mode and Dawn Mode. Dawn Mode's build arrives before the day everyone gets. The message is light arriving: you see the day first.

Yūgen The art says which build you are in, in one look. A dawn sky on a horizon: night still at the top with its last stars, plum, apricot, gold at the horizon, and thin cloud bands lit from below. The sun coming up is kansō's ensō. Five colours of its own per theme: dawn-top, dawn-mid, dawn-low, dawn-edge, dawn-sun. One image per theme, drawn by us.
Kansō One home: the sidebar header, 56 high, behind the lights and above the tools. Nothing in the footer, nothing anywhere else.
Kansō It is a piece (board 10): Artwork, the default in Dawn Mode; Pill, "Dawn Mode" at the right of the lights, tinted with dawn-sun; or Hidden. Stable Mode shows nothing.

Seijaku The sun comes up once: when the window opens in Dawn Mode, and at the moment you switch to it. The sky lightens from the horizon over 2.6 s, the sun rises to its place, the ensō draws itself as it arrives, the cloud bands light last. Then it is still for the session. Reduced motion shows the final frame. Every copy of the band plays together.
Shizen Risk in words, before the press. The switch's row says "It can break" under it; one press switches. A release that breaks something says so first in What's new.
Shizen In Dawn Mode (board 11), as every sidebar board that follows.
Shizen The sidebar of board 01, at full height. Every row the app has, in its place, on the 01 grid: leads 15, names 8 after, a level every 23, rows 32 (50 with a second line), groups 12 apart.

Kansō At rest a row is its lead, its name and its ensō. A second line only when needed (working, blocked), and the user chooses (board 10). + and ⋯ on the row under the pointer; no chevron, the row folds (S04).
Kansō A computer says its state in a word on its row (Off, Unreachable) with its one fix as a row button (power, refresh). Never a block under the row (S21).
Yūgen Asleep is one folded group with its count; a project in it wakes from its row (S07).
Seijaku Nothing moves: a row keeps its height and a name its width under the pointer, on focus and on a state change. Motion is the ensō spin and the working name's shimmer, nothing else.
Kokō Colour only for a state, on the mark. Counts (↓12, 2) are muted.

Kansō The title bar is the lights, 48 high, with Dawn Mode's band behind them (11). Under it the tools row, 40: + at the left; sort, search and hide at the right. Chrome buttons, 32 with 17, muted, foreground under the pointer. All four are there at rest; each says what it does in a tooltip.
Seijaku + means the same in every view: a conversation in a project you pick, then New project…, Open a folder…, Add computer…. A project chosen asks which agent (S14).

Kokō Sort keeps only orders. Away from its default it stays foreground and its tooltip names the order; no dot, no badge. The Show switches it repeats live in Settings · Pieces and in right-click (10).
Yūgen Search opens find in place (S13), not a second list in a dialog. Hide folds the sidebar to the rail (S12).

Seijaku The kit's segmented control, 30, under the tools row and 12 above the list, spanning the list's width (8 in from each side), like the rows under it. Track w4, the chosen segment w12, no edge, 12.5 medium (K).
Kokō No dot. A waiting agent is said by its row and by the status bar; a dot here was a third, wordless copy. The Needs you section says it with the mark and the words in foreground, not in red.
Yūgen The keys live in the tooltip: ⌃⌥P, ⌃⌥S, ⌃⌥T (view-spaces|agents|threads).
Kansō It is a piece (10): Hidden, the list starts under the tools and stays on Projects; Status and Threads keep their keys. Collapsed, the same three stand as icons in the rail (S12).

Seijaku A project row is 32: the name 13.5 semibold, then its folder, branch and ahead/behind as a tail, 11.5 dim with the counts muted, as in 01. No initial tile: the rail keeps the letter, where it is the only name.

Kansō A worktree is a sibling checkout, not something the project spawned: its branch mark as lead, its name muted, one level under the project, no elbow. With one agent it is that agent's row, the branch dim after the name. With none, or two or more, it keeps its own row.
Kansō ↑N shows only while no pane of that place is in view; an open pane's header already says its commits. ↓N stays: nothing else says behind upstream, and you act on it.

Shizen + stays on the active project; on every other row + and ⋯ come with the pointer. The row itself folds; folded, it shows what it hides in place of any chevron: the most urgent mark and how many.

Kansō ↓N pulls on one press (git pull --ff-only, undoable, so it never arms): marked at once (↓N goes, a breathing dot, the tooltip says Pulling) and quiet until git answers. A refusal brings ↓N back and says why in a toast (S21).

Kansō A failed read is a word on the row (S21): Folder not found, with Locate as the row's button; the path and Explain in right-click (10). Under an unreachable computer the rows stay dim, with when they were read, once the computer's line is opened (S06).
Yūgen Kept with nothing open is one muted row; a click asks which agent starts there (S14). Double-click renames in place; Enter keeps, Esc leaves. The keyboard ring is the kit's focus ring (K).
Kokō Cost: git status and rev-parse per place when a folder changes or a turn ends; remote places once a minute, in front only. Hidden git (sidebar.git) runs nothing.

Seijaku A row is 32: the program's icon 15 (a terminal's is Lucide's terminal), the name 13.5 medium 8 after, its ensō 14 at the right. With a second line, 50. One weight always, so a change of state never reflows the name.

Shizen The second line is the user's choice (right-click, 10): What it is on, Time in its state and Commands still running, each Show, Only when needed or Hide. At Only when needed, the default: a working or blocked agent shows what it is on · its time; a finished one shows the count of commands still running, named in the tooltip; an idle one is its name.
Kokō Ink: working, blocked and focused in foreground; finished and idle muted; a sub-agent dim. The state lives on the mark alone: blocked on the ensō, the question in foreground, never red.
Fukinsei Under the pointer pin and ⋯ take the time's place; the mark never moves. A pinned row keeps a 12 pin before its mark. The keyboard ring is the kit's focus ring (K).
Kansō Sub-agents sit under their parent, their icon under its name, joined by the tree line (01). A sub-agent that needs you says it with its own mark and line; folded, the parent shows it (S04).

Yūgen A terminal has no ensō: it has no turn to report. In Status and Threads, mixed lists, the project (and the computer when it is not this one) follows the name in dim; in Projects the rows above say it. Under an unreachable computer the row is dim with an idle ensō; the computer's line says why (S06).
Seijaku Motion: the ensō spin and the working name's shimmer. No counting dots.
Kokō Cost: the step and the question come with Herdr's own report (OSC 7501), zero commands. Running commands: one local ps while an agent works, none when sidebar.tasks is hidden.

Seijaku A computer is a row like any other (01): its icon 15 as lead (monitor for this one, server for a remote), its name 13.5 medium, its state in a word at the right (11.5 dim) and its one fix as a row button, 20 with 12. The projects that live there follow under it.

Kansō Off, Unreachable and Needs login are one word on the row, never a block under it (S21): Off with power (a choice, not a failure), Unreachable with Refresh, Needs login with Sign in, which opens a terminal pane running hc machine login dark. The source's words, the other fixes and Explain to <agent> live in right-click (10). Opened, an unreachable computer shows its projects dim, as last read.
Shizen Said once: a computer that drops while you are here is a toast with Refresh; then its row says Unreachable and nothing else repeats it.

Kansō Turn on is one press, marked at once: the row is on, its projects are the kit skeleton until hc answers; a refusal turns it back and says why in a toast. Connected, the row holds power, + and Sync under the pointer; Sync's mark stays while it is on, and when it can't run the row says so in a word with Sync as its button.

Yūgen Folded, the row shows the most urgent mark and how many projects (S04). With no project it is the kit empty: No projects on dark yet, New project. Double-click renames in place, an alias kept by kansō and carried by Sync.

Kokō Cost: hc machine ls every 30 s in front, 2 min behind; a dim computer is read once a minute only while opened; one caffeinate hold per connected computer every 270 s; Sync one exchange per 3 min per computer it is on for. Off: nothing.

Kansō Asleep is one folded row at rest, with its count (S04). Open, its rows are 32 one level in: the name dim, Wake at the right as a quiet link; no moon, the group says it. Enter on the row wakes; the menu stays on right-click. The count shows only when folded, where the rows can't be seen.
Shizen Sleep and Wake are one press, marked at once (S21): the row moves and shows the breathing dot until it lands. Wake on the row is the undo. No breathing moon, no "Going to sleep", no spinner.
Kansō Could not sleep is a word on the row (S21): Couldn't sleep, with Undo as the row's button (the tab comes back as it was); the reason and Explain in right-click (10). No toast repeats it.

Yūgen On an unreachable computer the row stays, dim, with when it was read, and no Wake: it can't run there now. A tab asleep in an awake project is one row named by the tab, Wake N; its agents fold under it. A whole project asleep keeps its moon: among awake projects it is what tells it apart.
Kokō Cost: none at rest. A sleep or wake runs where the project lives, when you ask.

Yūgen A card, not a list header: raised on the sidebar's chrome, radius 8, a 1 px border, 4 inside. It is the one raised surface in the sidebar, so it reads as a note left for you; when there is nothing new it takes zero space.
Seijaku It docks at the foot of the list, 12 above the footer, over empty space: no row moves when it comes or goes, and the list keeps its place.

Seijaku On the 01 grid: the title row 32, "While you were away" 13.5 semibold with × (20 with 12) at its right. Each event a row of 32 (50 with a detail line): its icon 15 in its state colour, the fact 12.5 with the name medium, the detail 11.5 muted, the time 11.5 dim at the right. Four rows, then "+N more".

Kansō It lists only what nothing in view says: a merge, an approval, a red check out of view, an agent that went to sleep or could not, an agent whose pane is gone. A PR verdict in a pane header in view, or an agent still on screen, is not repeated (L).

Shizen A click opens the thing (the pane, the PR panel on the step, the Wake menu) and drops the row. × dismisses the batch. Right-click: Dismiss these, then the piece lines (10); Hide this switches it off for good, the same switch as its row in Settings · Pieces (sidebar.away: Show, When needed, Hide).
Kokō Cost: none. Events come from what kansō already reads; they are written to the local database.

pages.page: Compositions/Needs you list: hidden by default
guidelines: Kansō Hidden by default (sidebar.needs). Nothing is lost: the row keeps its mark and its question (S05), the status bar names the oldest one with +N while its row is out of view (L), Status opens on the same list, and ⌘J walks the waiting agents.
Shizen Only agents that wait count. A finished agent is not Needs you: its word is Finished, on its row.

Seijaku Shown, it is a section of the same rows (the mark and the words Needs you as its head, the project after each name in dim), not a second component with sizes of its own. It appears only with rows and never replaces the list. Nobody waiting draws nothing.
Kokō Cost: none. It reads what Herdr reports.

Kansō Sections in order of what they ask of you: Needs you, Working, Done, Idle, Asleep, Terminals. A head is 32, 13.5 strong muted, words only; Needs you keeps its mark, the words stay muted (Kokō: colour on the mark). No chevron: the head folds, and folded it shows its count (S04). Idle, Asleep and Terminals start folded; what you have to act on starts open.

Seijaku The rows are S05's rows, flush at 8: the program's icon, the name, the project after it in dim (and the computer when it is not this one: ops · dark), the ensō at the right. The second line comes as the user chose (10): at Only when needed, on working and blocked agents. Sub-agents keep their tree line under their parent (01).
Kokō Projects have no colours of their own: colour is for agent state. The six hues were raw hex outside the theme.
Yūgen Empty is the kit's (S21): the view's icon and one sentence, no action, since + is right above. First read is the kit skeleton, breathing, at the rows' height.
Shizen Sort (S02): latest change first, longest in its state, project.
Kokō Cost: none of its own. It draws what Herdr reports; the step comes with the agent's report.

Seijaku A conversation is a row like any other (S05): the program's icon, its title, its ensō, 32. What it says now, or your last message as "You: …", is the second line, as the user chose (10): at Only when needed, on the ones working or waiting.

Kansō Grouped by project (default): the project's name heads its conversations, a head of 32 in muted words; its + comes with the pointer, as in Projects. Pinned first. Snoozed and Settled start folded with their count; no chevron, the head folds (S04). Open, a snoozed row's time is when it comes back (Thu 9:00).
Kokō A snooze that ended says Woke as a word after the title, dim, as Off on a computer: no pill, no accent. Colour stays on the mark.

Kansō A conversation that can't be read is a word on the row (S21): Can't read, with Refresh as its button; the read's words and Explain in right-click. Empty is the kit's: the view's icon and one sentence.
Shizen Under the pointer a finished row shows Settle (✓) and ⋯; Pin, Snooze and Mark unread are in the menu (S18).
Kokō Cost: transcripts on this computer, read every 60 s (15 s while Threads is in front), only files that grew. Other computers' conversations are not read: zero remote calls.

Kansō Search opens a find field in place of the switch, under the tools row: the kit's field, 30 tall, canvas, the kit's focus ring while it has the keyboard, placeholder Find, esc at its right. Esc closes it and the list comes back as it was. ⌘F and / from the list open it too.

Shizen The list itself narrows: projects, worktrees, agents, conversations and asleep rows that match by name, step, branch or folder; the project stays as context. The matched letters go foreground semibold; nothing else changes, nothing moves.
Yūgen The first match carries the keyboard ring: Enter goes there, ↓ ↑ move, the list keys work as in S17.

Kansō It works on what the sidebar already knows, rows on other computers included (dim when unreachable, with when they were read). No match is the kit empty (S21): the search icon, one sentence with what you typed, no action.
Kokō Cost: none. It filters what is drawn; it asks nothing of any computer.

pages.page: Compositions/New project, new conversation, new worktree
guidelines: Kansō Every start ends in one menu, "New in kansō": the agents installed on that computer with their own marks, the one used last there marked last, then Terminal, then In a new worktree…. Nothing is started for you. While the agents are asked for, the kit's skeleton rows breathe and Terminal is ready at once; none found is one dim line naming the computer, and Terminal.

Seijaku Dialogs follow the kit: 24 inside, title 15 semibold, labels 12.5 muted, fields 30 on canvas, and the kit's footer at the right, 8 apart (D1): Cancel quiet, the action solid. No caption under the title that teaches; Esc closes. The primary is solid, never accent.

Shizen Create is one press and optimistic: disabled until there is a folder; the name follows the folder until you type one; pressed, the dialog closes and the row is in Projects at once with the breathing dot until the database answers (S21).

Kansō A refused write keeps the dialog and puts the kit failure block under the fields (S21, the block form: a dialog has the room): the tool's words, then the action's own name (Create) and Explain to <agent>; the footer keeps Cancel only. "Already a project" and "already checked out" put the fix in slot one: Go to it, Open it.
Yūgen The worktree's folder is shown as a fact in mono before you create it; git's refusal uses the same block.
Kokō Cost: asking which agents are installed runs one command in that computer's shell (remote for a remote project), only when the menu opens.
Kansō kansō's own dialog in the kit, opened from + → Add computer… and from a computer's menu. It runs the same hc machine add Herdr's dialog runs; the word is computer, never machine.

Seijaku Hosts from ~/.ssh/config as rows of 32: the server icon, the name, how ssh reaches it in mono dim, and Add at the right as the kit's small tonal button. A typed user@host goes in the field below; Enter adds.

Shizen Add is one press and optimistic: the row says Added at once, with the done mark and the word in muted, and stays quiet until ssh answers. A refusal clears it and puts the kit failure block under that host's row (S21, the block form: a dialog has the room): ssh's own words, then the action that fits (Sign in, a terminal pane running the login, or Add) and Explain to <agent>.

Yūgen After a Mac is added, the one fact that will matter: it asks before agents read Documents, with the button that opens that setting there. No paragraph explains it. No hosts is the kit empty, one sentence; the field below is the action.
Kokō Cost: reading the ssh config is local. Each Add is one ssh connection, when you press it. Nothing at rest.

Seijaku The row held stays where it was, on the pressed wash (w12); where it will land is a 2 px accent line at a row's top or bottom. No ghost, nothing resizes, nothing else moves (Herdr draws no ghost; neither do we).
Kansō Projects move within their computer only (Herdr's own rule); outside it no line is drawn, so nothing promises a drop.
Shizen An agent can be dragged in any order. The first drop switches the project to Your order and the sort icon turns foreground (S02). Pinned rows move among the pinned; a drop renumbers the pins.
Kansō A pane held in the strip and let go over the sidebar goes back where it was: no mark on the sidebar.
Kokō Cost: none; a drop writes a label (pins) or a preference.
Kokō One ring: the kit's focus ring (K), 2 px accent outside the row, the same on every control of the app. Never a second wash; the selection wash stays where it was.
Kansō It walks every row in screen order: computers, projects, agents, sub-agents, asleep rows. Nothing is skipped and nothing is special.

Fukinsei The panels' keys: j k or ↓ ↑ move, gg G go to the ends, Enter or l runs the row's first action (focus the pane, fold or go, Wake, the row button of a failed computer), Esc returns to the pane you came from, / opens find (S13).
Seijaku The ring leaves when the list loses the keyboard (a click on a pane). No hint on screen: the keys live in Settings · Keys and the palette.
Kokō One menu, the kit's (10): 252 wide, rows 30, icons 14 muted, an 11.5 dim head naming what was clicked. Hints at the right in dim (when, where, last).

Kansō Twelve rows, not twenty-four. Snooze, Move to project and Copy open their own short popup (›) instead of five presets, a project list and three copies inline. Sleep its project lives in the project's menu, its one home. Settle appears on Threads only.
Seijaku Every menu ends the same way: the piece lines of the thing under the pointer, Hide “…” and Settings for this… (10).
Kansō Armed in place. Close agent and Remove project become "Press again …" on accent for 4 s, the kit's Armed (K), and the menu stays open. Remove says how many tabs close.
Seijaku One word for each thing: New conversation (the + says the same), Sleep the project, Wake all 3 in review.
Kansō A computer answers a right-click too: Rename, Turn off, Sync, New project, Add computer. The asleep row's menu leads with Wake; Everything asleep… opens the Sleep dialog.
Seijaku One row on the 01 grid: Settings, 32 with its gear 17 muted and 13.5 text, 8 above and 16 below. The block is its rows (56; 88 with an update row), never a fixed band with empty space above.

Kansō One door to settings. Settings opens the kit menu (252, rows 30): kansō settings (⌃⇧, opens it directly) and Herdr settings (Herdr's own window). The tab bar's gear goes. Herdr's logo is not an icon anywhere in the footer or the rail.
Kansō Dawn Mode puts nothing here: its one home is the header band (11, S02). The footer reads the same in Stable Mode and Dawn Mode.
Kokō An update is words, in foreground: one row above Settings, "Update kansō to 3.31.0" with the refresh icon, or in Dawn Mode "Update to 3.31.0-beta.3". No dot beside words that already say it.

Shizen Update is one press, marked at once (S21): the row reads "Updating kansō" in muted, no spinner, quiet until it lands. Refused: the row returns and the kit failure block sits under it, aligned with the words: the tool's own line, then Update and Explain to .

Kansō Herdr's own update lives in that menu: when one waits, a third row "Update Herdr to 0.1.16" after a rule. It restarts the window, so it arms first ("Press again to restart Herdr", 4 s); terminals live in herdr-core and stay.

Kansō The account chip goes (L): its count is the status bar's, its name is you, its click was the Settings row's. Add computer moves to the + menu (S02) and hides with its piece; the rail drops its square too.
Kokō Cost: none here; the update check is the tab bar's.
Seijaku First read is the kit skeleton (K): projects and their agents as S01 draws them, a name, a name and its ensō, at 32, breathing. Rows replace it as they come; nothing jumps.
Yūgen No project is the kit empty (S21): one dim sentence and one action, New project. No sentence explaining what a project is.

Shizen Narrow, nothing reflows: under 240 wide rows keep their first line only, the waiting one too (its wash and mark still say it); a branch after a name truncates first; the switch keeps its three words at 12.5. Under 160 it folds to the rail (S12) and opens again at the width you had.
Kokō Cost: none of its own.
Seijaku Every element sits where the app draws it; the redesign goes on top. Width 76; the first 48 are the lights, with Dawn Mode's band behind them, 56 high, cut to the rail around its centre (11).

Kansō Chrome in the kit's squares: show-sidebar first, centred on the line Herdr's logo held (its 32 square starts at 50), then + 8 below, both 32 with 17 (01). The view switch under them keeps its place and loses the blocked dot (S03). Herdr's logo is not an icon in the rail.

Seijaku Tiles on the grid: the list starts 8 below the switch; a project is a 40 tile, radius 6, 4 apart, its initial 13.5 strong 2 above its count 11.5. A computer is its 15 icon; a remote one is dim while it can't be read, its projects folded under it until it is opened; this computer has no glyph, the list starts with its projects (S01). Before a remote computer a 24 hairline in border at 50%, centred, taking no height: decorative, so no contrast rule (A).

Kokō Each project keeps the colour the app gives it (avatarColor from assignColors: ansi6, ansi3, ansi4, ansi5, ansi2, ansi1, least used first, kept in space.colors). In the kansō themes ansi1 to ansi5 are blocked, done, working, blue and violet; ansi6 has no token, so the board mixes blue and done half and half. A kept project with nothing open stays muted. The open sidebar has no initial (S04): the letter and its colour live here, where they are the only name.
Kokō An unread or woken row is a foreground count: the initial already carries the project's colour and the accent ring belongs to the keyboard (K).
Kansō Footer square: Settings only, the gear, opening the one settings menu (S19); Add computer is in the + menu. The block is its rows (56; 88 with an update row), as S19.

Yūgen Tabs carry no program icon and no working mark: the pane headers carry both, and the icon told no tab apart. A mark shows only when it asks or changed: Needs you, and Finished until seen. Piece tabs.marks, S.

Kansō Close stays where it is: × on the active tab, at rest. On a tab that holds an agent the first press arms it for 4 s: the tab turns accent in its own box and the tooltip says "Press again to close checkout". Nothing changes width. A plain shell closes on one press.
Kansō Double-click renames in place with the built-in Input, name selected. Enter keeps it, Esc puts it back. The dialog with its hint goes.
Kokō Drag: the held tab stays on the pressed wash (w12, as S16) and a 2 px accent bar shows where it lands.
Shizen A rename on another computer is drawn at once: the new name at 80% with a breathing dot until the core confirms. Refused, the old name comes back and the toast says so (B9).
Kansō The " Z" after a zoomed tab's name goes. The zoomed pane fills the tab and its header holds Unzoom.
Shizen Tabs that do not fit fold behind +5, which opens them as a menu with their marks. + and Arrange sit outside the scroller.
Shizen devbox connecting: one breathing skeleton per known tab. Unreachable: tabs at 55% (S21 stale), and no +, because it cannot start anything there.
Kokō Remote: 0 calls at rest. Tabs come over the core's own link.

Seijaku Measured, unchanged: bar 48 (layouts/kanso.json:62), px 12, no fill of its own (tabs/main.js:406). A tab is 26 tall, 8 inside, 8 between icon, name and mark, text 12.5, icon 15, mark 14, name up to 170; 2 between tabs, 8 to + and Arrange. Panel buttons 26 with 2 between (:386, :418); the last one now sits 12 from the edge.
Seijaku One button for all: 26 square, icon 15, hover w7, open w12. The name is the tooltip, with its key. Nothing changes width, so no button moves when you point at one or open one.
Yūgen A closed panel button paints nothing: no fill, no border, the frame shows through. Only hover and open paint.

Kansō The ? and the gear leave the tab bar and its end closes up. Settings has one door: the footer's Settings row, whose menu holds kansō settings (⌃⇧,) and Herdr settings (S19). The ? opened the same dialog on Keys, so it was a second door; ⌘⇧/ still opens Keys.
Kokō Drag to reorder shows the held button on the pressed wash and the accent bar, as tabs do.

Yūgen Panels is the place a hidden panel comes back from: a check means shown, the key is ⌃⇧N in bar order, hover shows the grip, and a row drags to reorder. Hiding unmounts the panel, so its reads stop.
Shizen Fold order as the bar narrows: tab names to 120, then to 72, then extra tabs into +N. Panel buttons, + and Arrange never fold: they stay visible at any width.
Seijaku Window buttons are icons in the same 26 button, not "−" and "□" in the font, right after the panel buttons.

Seijaku Order: Files, Spend, PR, Shipped, Worktrees, Ports, Containers, Memory, Images, then Simulator when a simulator tool exists (tabs/main.js:57-68), until the person drags them (:72-77). The boards draw the default.
Kokō Remote: 0. A hidden panel mounts nothing.
Seijaku kansō draws it with the one menu (252, rows 30, radius 8).
Seijaku The header names where the tab opens: the project, plus the computer when it is not this one.
Kansō Only installed agents, keyed 1 to 9. "not installed" rows were dead controls and they go.
Kansō "New space" stays, worded New project as everywhere. "Start an agent" goes: the icons say it.

Seijaku Checking again keeps the last list usable and spins a 12 ensō in the header. With no list yet, it shows two skeleton rows. A timeout is the state pattern's BLOCK (S21, state.css) in the agents' place: "Can't list agents on devbox", the tool's words as evidence, then Refresh and Explain to api.
Yūgen Worktree rows show only inside a repository. Arrange is the last row, ⌥⌘T: it left the tab bar (B12).
Kokō Remote: one agent check on the project's computer per open, and the last answer paints at once. 0 at rest.
Yūgen Hover shows four tools, not eight: split right, width, close, and ⋯, which opens the pane menu (board B10). Pin, open with, split down and send live there. 26 buttons with 15, 2 apart (01).
Seijaku The focused finished or idle pane keeps Sleep and Send visible (board 03). A blocked pane has no Send.
Shizen A blocked header loses the words "Needs you": the agent's row says it. The 40% blocked wash, the breathing bar and the mark stay.

Seijaku One spacing rule for every header on these boards: the header alone, 34 tall, its content centred with equal room above and below. Where the pane matters, the line under it is terminal text, never an empty band.
Kansō Close arms when the pane holds an agent: the × turns accent in its own 26 box and the tooltip says "Press again to close tests" (4 s). Nothing moves.
Kansō Pinned is a 12 pin in dim after the name, and no grip. The accent wash goes: accent is the window asking.
Yūgen The grip has no tooltip. The grab cursor says it.
Kansō Double-click renames in place, as tabs do. The dialog with its hint goes.
Shizen The blocked bar breathes on battery too.

Yūgen Moving a pane: every terminal in the tab gives way to a card, icon 17 and name 13.5, so the whole pane takes the drop. The held one stays on the pressed wash (w12, as S16). The target splits toward the side under the pointer and shows the held pane there in accent 25%, the same wash as the header zone, not accent 40. Below also lights the pane's foot (the ruler, :265-292).
Kansō On another computer: the folder is shortened with that computer's home, so it reads ~/acme-shop, not /home/jj/acme-shop. The computer's name is not repeated on every header.
Seijaku Unreachable: name, icon and digest at 55% as last read (S21 stale), no state mark (it is unknown), terminal at 55%. The words live on the sidebar row and the status bar.

Yūgen GitHub not answering: the PR segment's place takes the state pattern's LINE (S21): mark, "Can't read #142", a small Refresh. The tool's words are in the tooltip. A click opens the PR panel on its BLOCK of the same words.

Seijaku Its grid: 34 tall, 12 left and 8 right, 8 between items, text 12.5, top radius 8, icon 15, name up to 260, folder and branch 11.5 with a 12 icon, up to 220, mark 14, the grip a 14 icon in a 20 box. On the right: tools, then the mark, then the grip.
Kokō Remote, per stop: git status --porcelain=v2 --branch and git diff --shortstat (two calls, down from four), plus one gh pr view per distinct branch. 0 at rest.

pages.page: Compositions/Pane header, folding as the pane narrows
guidelines: Shizen The tools are on every header at rest, as an action is (B4). As the pane narrows, information folds before any action: folder, then branch. Then the tools fold into ⋯ (the pane menu, which holds every one of them), with close staying out. Then commits, files, the verdict word (#142 keeps its colour) and the PR segment. Then close joins ⋯, and the name truncates.
Seijaku Never folded: program icon, state mark, grip, ⋯.
Yūgen A folded segment keeps its fact in the PR segment's tooltip, word for word (one prLine).
Seijaku Replaces board 03. The same ten states and the same segments, drawn with the header spacing of B4.
Kansō The 6 px dot beside the verdict goes. The verdict is already a word in its colour: blocked for failed, conflicts and changes requested, working for running and behind, done for ready.
Shizen Needs you is the blocked wash, the breathing bar and the mark (B4).
Kansō Kept: the shimmer. Removed: the counting dots after a working name. The battery branch at :362 also drops the shimmer, against "motion never stops"; the build removes that branch too.
Kokō Remote: as B4. One gh pr view per distinct branch when an agent stops, and every 60 s only while a check is pending.
Fukinsei It opens under the focused pane's header, right-aligned, 420 wide: next to what it searches, not in the middle of the window.
Kansō A row shows the time only. The day is its header, so "2026-11-11 14:02" on every row goes.
Seijaku Previous and Next are drawn in dim while there is nothing to move to.

Seijaku Failure and empty use the state pattern (S21, state.css) where the matches start. A missing file is the BLOCK: "Can't read checkout's conversation", the path as evidence, Refresh, Explain to checkout. No matches is the EMPTY plate with the search icon, and the count slot stays empty.
Seijaku A plain shell gets the terminal's own search.
Kokō Remote, on devbox: one read when it opens, then one when the agent stops or you press Enter.

pages.page: Compositions/Menus of the bars and headers
guidelines: Seijaku One menu for every right-click and popup in the bars: kansō's own, 252 wide, rows 30, radius 8 (K), icons 14 in muted, keys 11.5 in dim, the header 11.5 dim naming what was clicked. It replaces Herdr's menu for tabs (31, radius 7) and its new-menu.
Yūgen Order everywhere: the thing's own actions, then the act that ends it, then the piece lines (Only when needed when the piece has it, Hide this, Settings for this…).
Kansō An act that ends agents arms in place for 4 s and names what it ends: "Press again to close 2 agents".

Kansō Pane menu: grouped by kind, with a header. Split left stays in the menu, with ⌥⌘⇧D shown. "Send right-clicks to pane" and "Use Herdr right-click menu" become one checked row, "Right-clicks go to the program". Find in conversation and Sleep join. Rows that cannot act are not drawn.
Seijaku Separators come from groups, not from a row's index (menu/main.js:78).
Seijaku The PR segment and panel button menus are board 10's, unchanged.
Seijaku Keys: j k gg G Enter Esc, as in panels. Nothing is chosen until you move.
Kokō Remote: 0. Pin state and agents are read from the window.
Kansō The branch leaves the bar. Its homes are the pane header (the pane's) and the project row (the project's). The bar said it a third time.

Kansō Information and actions are told apart. The computer's name is information: it shows only while the sidebar's computer row is out of sight. Needs you, an action, always shows while someone waits. A computer you know is down is said once, by a toast when it drops (B9); after that the bar names it only while a pane of that computer is in front, because then it explains what you are looking at.

Shizen The computer, piece status.computer S/N/H, default N: the name while the sidebar row is out of sight; "Can't reach devbox" with a small Refresh while a pane of devbox is in front. A click on either reconnects; while it waits, "devbox" is drawn pending (80% and a breathing dot) until it answers.

Seijaku Needs you, piece status.needs N/H, default N: drawn while any agent waits. Mark, name, question, +1. The question comes from the row's own function, so it is the same words and the same cut. Click: ⌘J.
Kansō The working count, piece status.agents S/N/H with default N: drawn only while one works. "4 agents idle" and "No agents" go. Click opens the sidebar on Status.
Kokō Memory, ports, containers, reviews: as board 05. Memory is this computer's guard file, read every 60 s on this computer only.

Kansō Fold order, right half: the palette key goes first, then the count becomes its number, then servers, containers and reviews become their icon (the words move to the tooltip), then the question shrinks to nothing, then Memory becomes "8% free". The name and +1 never fold, so no fact leaves the bar. Left: the computer becomes its icon.

Seijaku Its grid: 26 tall, 12 inside, 16 between items, text 11.5, icons 14 with 8 between, mark 14. Two halves of equal weight around the strip's fixed 180 minimap slot (layouts/kanso.json:127-160), so the map stays at the centre whatever each side says, and each half folds in its own width, (window − sidebar − 180) / 2.
Kokō Remote at rest: 0 for computer, needs you, count, memory, palette. Ports every 120 s and reviews at most every 120 s, both only with the window in front. Hide stops them.

Kansō Edges show which panes are past them: chevron, then tiles 20 with the program icon. Click a tile to go there, hover for its name. The state dots on the tiles go: the sidebar rows and the status bar already say who waits.
Kansō The hover card goes ("2 panes beyond the right edge" over a list of the same tiles). It was a hover card, which spec §7 rules out, and its title counted rows already in view.
Kokō A pane dragged over an edge washes it in accent 25%, as every drop zone does. Piece strip.edges, S/H, default S.

Yūgen Minimap, piece strip.minimap S/H, default S: it is a control (a pill jumps to its column, the stepper sets panes per view). Focused column fg, in view muted, out of view input, stacks as 2 px cells.

Kansō The "− 2 +" stepper stays on the bar. Its tooltips lose the teaching ("Fewer panes per view" becomes the key, ⌘⇧−). The right-click menu adds the same choice as a segmented control, and Even out.
Seijaku "Strip paused" becomes the state pattern's LINE: mark, "Layout paused", a small Resume. It still resumes alone after 10 s.
Kokō Remote: 0. Layout only.
Seijaku One shape, the menu's materials: popover, radius 8, the kit shadow. 360 × 40, mark 14, one sentence 12.5, and at most one action word, 12.5 medium. Up to three stacked, newest at the bottom.
Kansō A click goes to the fact. A word shows only for a different act: Undo, Update, Refresh, Restart, Open, Show, What's new.

Kansō The leading dot goes. A failure is the state pattern's toast (S21, state.css): the blocked mark, what failed in our words, one small button with the fix (Refresh for a read, the write's own name, Undo for a stuck sleep). The tool's words are in the tooltip. No Explain in a toast. The words match the BLOCK of the same failure.
Yūgen An echo shows only when its home is out of sight. PR: no header shows that PR. Update: the footer row is not on screen. Could not sleep: the Asleep group is not on screen.
Kansō On Dawn Mode the toast does not name the channel and wears no channel mark: the channel's one home is the sidebar header (board 11).
Kansō A computer that drops is said once, by this toast. Nothing stands on the bar after that unless a pane of that computer is in front (B8).
Kansō Share with nothing copied: one sentence naming the file and the post. The folder opens on its own, so the path line goes.
Kansō "Already a project" and "already has a worktree" leave the toasts. The New project and New worktree dialogs say it where you typed it (S14).

Seijaku One update checker remains: kanso-tabs/update.js, the only one that polls and installs, because the tab bar is always on screen. kanso-chrome/update.js, a byte-for-byte copy, is deleted. The footer row reads the shared kanso.update state and its press runs kanso-tabs.update, so each update toast has one sender.
Kansō Second sentences go: "Click to update; Herdr's own updates stay under Settings.", "Check it and post. Not there?…"

Yūgen System notifications: only while no kansō window is on screen. Otherwise the guard writes the notice and the window shows it as a toast in the same words. The memory notice uses the status bar's words, "Memory 8% free".
Seijaku Pieces: toast.agent S, toast.pr S, toast.update S, toast.memory S, plus guard.notify S for the system ones.
Kokō Remote: 0.

Seijaku Scope line 11.5 dim: the project, branch or computer, or what the page is. A stale read takes its place ("Read 14:02 · devbox unreachable · next try 14:07") and the body drops to 55%; writes are disabled.

pages.page: Panels/First screens: only what you would miss
guidelines: Kansō Subtract information, never options. At rest a panel drops facts that repeat or say nothing now: scope lines, second lines, labels, marks and colour with no reason. Those facts come back under the pointer or keyboard. Every action and option, those the app has and those we added, stays visible and one press away. Colour stays only on what asks for you, and failures stay loud.

Seijaku Measured in the browser on the six first screens: rows 103 → 76 · glyphs 35 → 19 · colours 33 → 25 · lines 150 → 88. Preview's 14 lines are the file itself, so its chrome is what halves: 2 rows to 1.

Kansō One fact, one place. The folder, branch, files and lines are in the pane header, so the panels drop their scope and facts lines. Header icons, the period switch, Reply and Comment fields, Everyone's, Explain, Remove all and Prune all stay.
Kansō Nothing is lost: each removed fact says where it lives now, and the options audit lists every control. Both are in panels-a-elements.md.
Yūgen At rest a panel shows what you would miss if it were gone. The rest appears when it matters: it needs you, it changed, or the pointer or keyboard is on it.

Shizen A second line appears on pointer or selection. Folds keep only their word.
Kokō Colour only on what asks: a stopped container, an agent that needs you, a size past the guard's limit, your own pins.

Seijaku Measured in the browser on the boards themselves: rows are the blocks stacked in the panel, lines are text lines, glyphs are icons and marks, colours are chromatic colours. The phone screen and the picture are content and are not counted.
Seijaku Rows fall less than half because most rows are the list itself: a port, a container, an agent. Those are the facts; none is dropped.
Shizen States that need you are unchanged; the failure, empty and pending screens on Q1 to Q6 stay as drawn.

Seijaku One menu (the kit's, 252 wide) from the header's share icon, in Ports, Memory, Spend and the hjkl dōjō. Its header is the privacy fact: "Counts and sizes only" (Ports, Memory), "Totals and days only" (Spend), "Scores and practice days only" (dōjō, shown once a round is played; D11 draws only the header icon).
Yūgen The icon shows only when there is something to share: history in Ports and Memory, an unfiltered home page in Spend.
Seijaku While the image is made, that row says so and the others dim; the result is the toast (B9).
Kansō The inline row of four bordered buttons and its sentence go (share.js:285-296).
Kokō Cost: none until chosen; then a local render. The post opens in the browser.
Seijaku One pin, everywhere a picture is shown: Simulator (iOS and Android), Images, Preview pictures (P05). Same marks, same note, same list, same Send.

Kansō Entering: on a live picture (Simulator) the Pin tool in the header, or ⌥P, because a click there is a touch on the device. The picture freezes on the frame you saw (the screenshot simctl or the emulator already gives) and the scope line says "frozen at 14:06:12". A 2 px focus ring marks the mode; the device's buttons are not drawn while frozen. The tool again, or Esc, returns to live. Where a click means nothing else (Images, Preview pictures) the pin is always on and there is no tool.
Seijaku Marks: a click drops a numbered pin; a drag draws a region, numbered at its corner. No strokes and no element picking: a device's picture has no DOM to pick from.

Kansō The note is typed beside its mark, at once: click, type, Enter; the next click starts the next one. A click on a mark edits its note; Backspace on an empty note removes the mark. The dialog goes.

Yūgen The list under the picture is the message, one line per mark, in the words that will be sent; × on hover removes one. One action: Send to checkout (the agent of the pane in front, named), ⌘↩. With none in front, Send to… opens the picker. It sends the frozen frame's path, the device and system, and the lines. After: "Sent to checkout 14:07", the marks clear, the picture is live again.

Kansō Unsent marks are kept per agent and picture when you leave, and the scope line says "kept from 13:52 · not sent". A rotation or a device change since the freeze is said once; the marks stay on the frame you saw. A stalled picture freezes on its last frame and says so.
Kansō An agent on devbox: the frame is copied there first, then the notes go with that path. Failures use the state pattern (S21): the source's words, then Send.
Seijaku Presses for one correction: the tool, a click, the words, ⌘↩. On Images and Preview: a click, the words, ⌘↩.

Seijaku Reused: pinFrom (look-model.js:50-54) for both marks; noted and aboutMessage (look-model.js:59-67), which gain a region form ("2 (region 3% to 97% across, 58% to 67% down)") and the device line; kept marks per agent and picture (look.js:277-286, 47); deliver and sendKey (deliver.js:11, 19); the waiting refusal (waitingNote, deliver.js:14); Send (look.js:457-478). New: the inline note (replaces the kanso-prompt overlay, look.js:417-442), drag regions, the frozen frame and ⌥P in kanso-sim, the copy to another computer, the shared classes.

Seijaku T3 Code annotates a live web page: picked elements, dragged regions, freehand strokes, one comment, a screenshot, then attach or send (contracts ipc.ts:816-948). kansō keeps its regions and its one-press send; it adds a note per mark, because a correction is usually several small things.

Seijaku A panel that needs a tool exists only where the tool does: docker for Containers, xcrun simctl or the Android SDK's adb for Simulator, macOS or Windows for Memory. Without it there is no button, no Settings row and no job.
Seijaku It replaces three sentences in empty panels: "Docker is not installed on this computer.", "Memory is not available on Linux." and Simulator's install rows.
Seijaku The probe runs once when the window starts and again when Settings opens, so installing Docker later brings Containers back without a restart of kansō.
Seijaku On a project that lives on another computer, Containers follows that computer's docker; Simulator and Memory stay on this one.
Yūgen The Simulator's rule, hidden when no tool is found, becomes the rule for all three.
Kokō Each surface's main state on the light theme: the same tokens, nothing new.
Seijaku Pictures and the device screen sit on raised inside the background slab, the step board 07 uses for the log card.
Kansō The armed Stop is accent on accent_foreground in both themes; no fixed white.
Seijaku The kit header: Files. Changed and All files are the two quiet words at its right, then Refresh. No scope line: the pane header already says the folder and branch.
Yūgen Opened from the digest's files segment it lands on Changed. From the tab bar it opens on the last view used. In a folder that is not a repository there is only the tree.

Seijaku The files the focused agent named come first, newest first, with no title: the panel opened from that agent. A named file that also changed carries its stat there and is not listed again. Named files that did not change sit on one dim line by name, each name a link. Also changed holds only the rest. The named part exists only for an agent pane with a conversation (piece files.named, S; Hide stops the transcript read).
Kansō No totals: the header's digest already says 3 files +42 −7. Each row carries its own stat.
Kansō Modified is the normal case and carries no mark. A and D sit where the file icon goes, dim; U alone is in blocked, because a conflict needs you. A folder shows how many changed files it holds.
Seijaku Rows 32, 12.5 type, 16 per level, selected on selected. j k move, Enter opens, Esc returns to the pane.

Seijaku A row opens the file in Preview. Its stat +14 −3 is a control too: it opens the diff (the PR panel's diff page, P10, read with git diff). Right-click gets a menu (Open the diff, Open, Open with…, Copy path) instead of going straight to Open with.
Seijaku The 500-per-folder cap is said inside the folder it cut, as a dim row. A folder that cannot be read says so in its own place.

Kokō Remote calls: none on this computer (a folder watch). On another computer, one tree read per open folder, then one stat every 5 s while the panel is in front, 30 s after three quiet reads, none when the panel is hidden.
Shizen First read: kit skeleton rows at 32, breathing. Later reads keep the rows and spin Refresh.
Yūgen Errors are the folder's own words in blocked, with Refresh, here and on another computer alike.
Seijaku Stale takes the scope slot: Read 14:02 · devbox unreachable · next try 14:03, rows at 55%. "Unreachable" is the sidebar's word for the same fact.
Seijaku A pane with no folder says so, instead of "No folder".
