Kokō Light: the same marks; only U is coloured. Selected rows use selected, never a hex.

pages.page: Panels/Preview: a text file, one save
guidelines: Seijaku The kit header: ‹ only when it came from Files or Images, the file name as the 20 title and its folder beside it, dim (the full path under the pointer). Open with and ✕ are its icons; ✕ closes the panel, besides its tab-bar button and Esc. Code is in ink with literals in muted: colour is kept for what asks for you.

Yūgen One save for every file. Save (⌘S) appears only while there is an edit, as the one solid button. Saving… holds its place, then "Saved" for 2 s. Markdown no longer autosaves here and not on another computer.
Kansō One press per decision, never "Press again". A programmer's editor: ⌘S saves, ⌘Z takes back. Nothing here asks twice; what could lose text gives an Undo after instead of a question before.
Shizen No Refresh icon. The file follows the disk on its own: with no edit open it shows the new text without a press.

Kansō Changed on disk while edited: one line with the time and two actions, one press each. Overwrite (also ⌘S) saves your text. Reload takes the disk's text. Either one leaves "Undo" on the same line (and ⌘Z) until the next edit, so neither text is lost.
Shizen The computer is gone: the edit stays, the line says so, and it saves on its own when the computer answers. No Retry to press.
Kokō Over 1 MB: the first 1 MB, read only, with "Cut at 1 MB" at the end (one read).
Seijaku Binary and gone say what the file is, with the action that still works.
Kokō Remote calls on another computer: one read to open, one write per Save (with the text it expects on disk), one stat every 5 s in front, 30 s after three quiet stats, none hidden.
Yūgen One click on a block edits it in place: the block takes the raised slab and the kit's focus ring. A click on a link still follows it.
Seijaku Clicking under the last block adds a paragraph.
Yūgen Source is a context icon in the header that stays lit while on, not a pill whose tooltip explains it. Its text is the file as written.
Seijaku Tables edit cell by cell. Add row, Add column and Remove row are quiet links under the table, so it is not covered in ✕ icons. Done closes it. Esc closes any block.
Shizen Save follows P03: ⌘S or the button, never on its own.
Seijaku Headings 20 and 15, body 13.5, code 11.5 on w7, so a document reads like the rest of the window.

pages.page: Panels/Preview: pictures, and the Load step
guidelines: Seijaku Pins are the one pin component (Fives, Q10: pbx-pin, pbx-reg, pbx-ov, pbx-pnote, pbx-plist, pbx-sent). On a picture a click means nothing else, so pin mode is always on and there is no tool: a click drops a numbered pin, a drag a region, the note is typed beside it, Enter ends it. The list under the picture is the message. Send to checkout (the agent of the pane in front), or ⌘↩, then "Sent to checkout 14:07". Presses: a click, the words, ⌘↩.
Yūgen The size in pixels shows under the pointer, beside the folder. The picture fits the width on canvas, radius 8.
Kokō Load is the one solid button and carries the cost: Load 4.2 MB. On a bad link the press is the decision, so the size belongs on the button and not in a line above it.
Shizen Loading keeps the picture's frame, breathing.
Seijaku Over 20 MB says what stops it, with Open with… beside it.
Seijaku Inside a note, a picture to load is one row: name, size, Load.
Kokō Remote calls: one stat to learn the size. Under 2 MB the copy starts at once. Over 2 MB nothing moves until Load.

pages.page: Panels/Pull requests: one list, by project
guidelines: One model. The panel is the list of open pull requests that concern you, and nothing else: no Closed tab, no merged rows, no inbox page, no "to review" pill, no switch pill. A merge is an event in While you were away.
Asked of you comes first, across every repository that asks you, sidebar project or not. The repository and who asked show on the row under the pointer or keyboard.

Then one group per sidebar project, in the sidebar's order, with the project of the pane in front first. A group holds your pull requests in that repository. Everyone's in acme-shop, a quiet link under the group, opens the others' under yours.

Inside a group, by status: changes requested or a failed check, then running, then ready, then draft. A row is one line: number, title, one word at the right. The word is coloured only when the row asks for you (failed, failing, changes, review, blocked); running, draft and approved stay dim.

The branch in front without a pull request gets the first row of its group: the branch, its one fact (2 commits not on GitHub, 3 behind GitHub, no pull request), and its one action, one press: Push, Pull or Create pull request (a page in the panel: title from the last commit, the body, Create or Create as draft; gh pr create --title --body --base --head). On the default branch there is no row.
The pane in front is not in git: nothing changes, the list is the panel. "No repository in ~/notes" is gone.

The branch in front has an open pull request: the panel opens on it, titled #142, with ‹ back. Its title, the verdict, the failing lines of the log (P07), Explain to checkout and Full log, then the Conversation (P16): each open thread as who, where and the question, your own reply folded, then its Reply field, Resolve and Explain; the Comment field closes the conversation. Details closes it with its summary; the repository, branch and lines are in the pane header. ‹ or Esc is the one step back to the list.
GitHub is the header's icon, and on a failed check Open log on GitHub stays beside Full log.
Rows are 32: number, title, one word. The state in full, the repository, who asked and the age show as a second line under the pointer or keyboard. A row opens that pull request, with ‹ back.

Remote calls: one GraphQL read per GitHub host, made on this computer. It holds asked-of-you and yours, with the review decision and the checks for each, and it replaces the two searches plus a gh pr list per project (up to 20). The status bar's "2 reviews" item shares it: at most every 120 s, only with the window in front and the panel or that item on screen, honouring GitHub's retry time. Opening the panel within 120 s of a read costs nothing. "Everyone's" is one gh pr list for that repository, when opened, kept until Refresh.

On another computer: GitHub is read from this computer, so the list costs devbox nothing. The branch row's facts are the header digest's git read that already runs there. Only Push and Pull call devbox.
Kansō The list is the panel. One list of open pull requests, by project; no hero, no scope line: the pane header already says the branch.
Yūgen The branch in front comes first. With no pull request its row leads and offers Create; with one, the panel opens on it (P07).
Seijaku Every row is the kit's two-line row: title 12.5, number and state as meta 11.5, the verdict word in its state colour and nothing else coloured (K, S21).
Kokō Cost: one gh pr list per project on open or Refresh; zero at rest (P06).
Seijaku The same three panels as 06, in light: the list on background, the log, threads and fields on canvas. State colours stay the state's; never a new red.
Seijaku The "Everyone's" group open, the review and every thread state are drawn in light on P16.

pages.page: Panels/Pull requests: every state of the list
guidelines: Seijaku First read: the kit skeleton in the list's shape. Later reads keep the rows and spin Refresh.
Seijaku Empty is one line, "Nothing open". If the branch in front has something to say, its row stays above it, and the line becomes "Nothing else open".
Seijaku Signed out and GitHub CLI missing are the only whole-panel states, and both are about this computer, which reads GitHub. Sign in opens gh auth login in a pane to the right.
Seijaku Rate limited and not answering use the kit stale line, with the last rows at 55%. Nothing retries sooner than GitHub's retry time.

Seijaku On devbox: the list doesn't change. The branch row names the computer, and Pull runs there. When devbox is unreachable, only that row dims, with the time it was read; the rest is GitHub's and stays live.
Shizen "Everyone's" reads in place: your rows stay and the others' rows breathe below them.

Kansō A pull request that asks you opens on Your review (P16): one field, Approve, Request changes, Comment. One that belongs to no pane explains to the agent of the pane in front, never a GitHub link.
Kansō A merged pull request leaves the list. Its branch row says so once ("#139 merged 14:20") until the branch changes, and offers Create pull request.
Shizen The branch's pull request paints at once from the header's read; only the card breathes.

pages.page: Panels/A pull request: every state says why
guidelines: Seijaku Every state that is not mergeable says why, on the card, in its source's words, and has one action that hands that reason to an agent: Explain to <agent>. One press sends the text on the card (plus the PR's URL) into that agent's prompt, and the button's place then says "Sent to billing 14:07".

Seijaku A reason the app found is handed over with Explain. "Explain to <agent>" carries the state, its source and the log; "Send to <agent>" stays for your own words (pins, notes). Two acts, two words.
Kansō The agent is the one in the pane on that branch. When no pane has the branch, it is the agent of the pane in front (here checkout). With no agent there, Explain is absent, never disabled.
Kansō Waits carry no Explain, because there is nothing to fix: draft (its action is Ready for review, one press), checks running, and "Checking whether it can merge".
Kansō Behind its base: Update branch is the primary, one press (GitHub can redo it), and Explain is beside it, quiet.
Yūgen Nothing ends in "Open on GitHub". GitHub is only the header's icon.

Kokō Where each reason comes from, all in the one gh pr view made on open or Refresh (zero extra calls at rest):
          
            mergeStateStatus and mergeable give the state.
      Seijaku statusCheckRollup gives each check's name, status and conclusion (FAILURE, CANCELLED, TIMED_OUT, ACTION_REQUIRED, SKIPPED) and its run, from which the log is read once.
      Seijaku reviewDecision, reviewRequests and latestReviews (with authorCanPushToRepository) give who was asked and who can merge.
      Seijaku viewerPermission gives your access.
      Seijaku baseRef.branchProtectionRule (requiredApprovingReviewCount, requiredStatusCheckContexts, requiresCommitSignatures) with the head commits' signature gives the unmet rules. Assumed readable with write access; when it is not, the line stays "Blocked by branch rules" with no list.
mergeStateStatus and mergeable give the state.
Seijaku statusCheckRollup gives each check's name, status and conclusion (FAILURE, CANCELLED, TIMED_OUT, ACTION_REQUIRED, SKIPPED) and its run, from which the log is read once.
Seijaku reviewDecision, reviewRequests and latestReviews (with authorCanPushToRepository) give who was asked and who can merge.
Seijaku viewerPermission gives your access.

Seijaku baseRef.branchProtectionRule (requiredApprovingReviewCount, requiredStatusCheckContexts, requiresCommitSignatures) with the head commits' signature gives the unmet rules. Assumed readable with write access; when it is not, the line stays "Blocked by branch rules" with no list.

Two reasons are local git, read once when the state turns, on the branch's computer against its last fetch: the conflicting files (git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only) and the missing commits (git log HEAD..origin/main). The failed log is one gh run view --log-failed per failure, cached.
Checks running re-read every 20 s only while the panel is open and in front.

pages.page: Panels/A pull request: sending, writing, elsewhere
guidelines: Seijaku Every detail page has ‹: one step back to the list. Reopen goes with the closed state; it lives on GitHub.
Kansō When the pane's agent is blocked, Explain is absent (never disabled), and the verdict line adds "· cart-ui needs you first". The log stays readable.

Kansō Explain to checkout (the one name for what was "Send to") sends on one press: the card is the text it pastes, so it needs no preview. Afterwards the button's place says "Sent to checkout 14:07".
Kansō Full log is a page in the panel (‹ back), from the --log-failed text already read; no new call. "Open log on GitHub" goes; GitHub is the header icon.

Kansō Explain goes to the agent the pull request belongs to (the pane on its branch); when it belongs to none, to the agent of the pane in front; with no agent there, the action is absent, never disabled.
Seijaku A refused write follows P00: gh's words where the actions were, then the action's own name to retry, then Explain.
Shizen Writing: the button keeps its size with "Merging…" and Refresh spins.

Kansō On another computer only the scope changes: GitHub is read and written from this computer; Explain goes to the agent on devbox. When devbox stops answering, the pull request stays live, and an Explain pressed then fails on P00's pattern: "Not sent: devbox unreachable", with Explain to checkout to try again. When GitHub stops answering, the stale line takes the scope slot and the writes are disabled (the stale line as drawn for the list on P06).
Shizen Narrow: title 15. The fold note drops the people count first.
Kokō Remote calls: a write is one gh call plus one re-read. Explain is a local deliver into the pane, no network.

pages.page: Panels/A pull request: Details open, and the pickers
guidelines: Kansō Details holds the rest, in this order: Description, People and labels, Checks, Unresolved threads (when there are any), Files, then Back to draft and Close. The other open pull requests are the list, one step back. Sections are titles only: no notes that repeat the verdict ("Changes requested" beside People) or the facts line ("1 failing · 4 passed", "3 · +86 −12").
Yūgen A people row is the control: a click on Reviewers opens its picker. It no longer needs a 22px tag icon that only shows in Details.

Kokō Every write here is optimistic and never blocks. A click marks the row at once (the kit's pending, S21: 80% and the breathing dot), the list stays live, and the next click lands immediately. The changes queue and leave together: 600 ms after the last click, one gh api graphql request with one aliased mutation per change (requestReviews with union, addAssigneesToAssignable or removeAssigneesFromAssignable, addLabelsToLabelable or removeLabelsFromLabelable). When GitHub confirms, the check goes full. A refused change puts its row back and shows gh's words on that row only (P00), with the action's own name to retry. Closing the picker or the panel never cancels the queue. Offline, the queue keeps and says so once.

Kokō The list itself comes from the local store at once. The skeleton shows only on the very first open of a repository, ever. It is refreshed behind, at most once per open, with one gh api graphql (labels or assignableUsers, 100).

Seijaku The local store: kdb.js:177 (Kdb, SQLite), schema at kdb.js:90-116, with pr_items (:108) and pr_fetches (:110). Added: pr_candidates (labels and people per repository) and pr_writes (the queue: url, kind, target, op, state, error, at).
Shizen Truncation is a fact: "First 100 of 132".
Seijaku Files use the Files panel's row: name, folder, stat, and a mark only for A, D or U. A row opens the diff page (P10).
Kansō Back to draft and Close: one press each, quiet, below a rule, then Undo where they were. Merge is the only second press in this panel.
Kokō Remote calls at rest: zero. Details reads nothing new; description, people and files come with the one PR read.

pages.page: Panels/A pull request: a file's diff, and comments on its lines
guidelines: Kansō A click on a diff line, or on the + that takes its number's place under the pointer, opens a comment field under that line. On your own pull request Comment (⌘↵) posts it at once: gh api graphql addPullRequestReviewThread (path, line, side, body). When a review is asked of you, the button is Add to review. The comment waits in the local store, drawn pending (S21), and goes with Approve, Request changes or Comment in one submit (P16).
Kansō Threads sit under their line in the diff too, with their Reply field: the same thread as in the conversation, never a GitHub link.
Seijaku Presses: a line comment from the pull request is 3 (the file in Details, the line, ⌘↵).

Yūgen A file's diff is a page: file name as the title, the PR, folder and stat as the scope, Open in Preview and Open on GitHub as the two icons. Lines 20 in mono 11.5, additions and removals washed in done and blocked at 12%. Files in P01 opens the same page for local changes.
Seijaku A file with no text diff says so in one line (P00's empty). Over 400 lines: P15.
Kokō Remote calls: a diff is one gh pr diff per pull request, run on this computer and cached until the pull request changes.

pages.page: Panels/A pull request: the conversation and the review, in the panel
guidelines: Seijaku Everything a review needs happens in the panel. GitHub is only the header's icon.

Shizen Conversation sits under the verdict and its action, in view, not inside Details. At rest each unresolved thread is its author, path:line and the comment in full; your own replies fold to "1 reply, yours". Its Reply field and Resolve and Explain are always there; under the pointer the 3 lines it sits on show (the commented one on w7). Then reviews and comments, oldest first, and the Comment field at the end.

Kansō Each thread offers Resolve (one press; it becomes one line with Undo) and Explain to <agent>. When the agent answers, its last words fill that thread's field, marked "webhooks answered 14:21"; ⌘↵ posts it.
Kansō When changes are requested, the reviewer's thread is the body: there is no separate comment card above it, so it is not drawn twice.

Kansō Asked of you: Files, then Your review: one field with Approve, Request changes and Comment. Line comments added on the diff page wait in the store, and go with the review in one submit; the count is the section's note.

Kansō Writes are optimistic (P00). A reply or a review appears in the conversation at once, pending (S21: 80% and the breathing dot), and goes full when GitHub confirms. If it is refused, it comes back out, the field keeps the text, and gh's words show under it with Reply. Offline, it waits, said once.
Kansō Presses: reply 2 (click the field, ⌘↵); resolve 1, Undo 1; comment 2; explain then post the agent's answer 2; review 2 (click the field, Approve).

Kokō gh calls. Reply: gh api graphql addPullRequestReviewThreadReply. Resolve and Undo: resolveReviewThread and unresolveReviewThread. Comment: gh pr comment --body-file -. Review with no line comments: gh pr review --approve, --request-changes or --comment. Review with line comments: one gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews carrying the event, the body and comments[].

guidelines: Seijaku The notes are a timeline: one line down the left, a node per release. Yours is filled and says you are here; releases above it are not installed yet; Dawn Mode builds have a node in dawn-sun.
Seijaku Version 15 and the date beside the node, relative and absolute (today · Nov 11). The one action, Update to 3.31.0, sits on its node.
Kansō Added, Changed, Fixed are quiet labels in a 64 column, said once per release beside the first of its lines, not headings that compete with the version.
Shizen Older releases fold to one line (version, date, how many changes) and open in place.
Kansō Updates (Stable Mode | Dawn Mode) and the version line with Refresh stay above it, as board 11. The automatic-check switch, the big Check button and the waiting banner stay removed.
Kansō Dawn Mode leaves the dialog clean: the band lives on the sidebar header (11), not on settings. The armed press confirms the channel; the band arrives there.
Kokō Remote: one GET of CHANGELOG.md and one git ls-remote --tags when the page opens or on Refresh; nothing while it stays open.

Kansō Rows are names only: Herdr, kansō, Lucide (ISC). What each is and the open-outside mark show on the row under the pointer; the row opens its page. The URL column, the avatars and the letter leads go.
Seijaku "Made by" becomes one line, Maintained by JJ, Iván Campaña, Leangseu Kim, Johannes Hund.
Kansō herdr-sim is removed: the Simulator has been kansō's own code since 3.31.0.
Kansō "kansō is a layout for Herdr, made in the open." goes: a caption.
Seijaku Nothing is downloaded: no avatars.
Kokō Remote: none.
Seijaku Help and Settings · Keys were two homes for which key does what. Help is now the Keys tab of kansō settings (D3), drawn here whole, dark and light.
Kansō
Seijaku The Guide's prose moves to the site's docs; every key it names is on the Keys page, and its two settings facts point at their homes (Herdr settings · Look, What's new).

Seijaku One shell for every dialog: popover, radius 8, padding 24 (K), 480 wide (popups 340). Title 15 semibold that names the thing (Rename checkout, not "Rename terminal"). An optional scope line, 11.5 dim, that is a fact. No paragraph, no label over a lone field.

Yūgen Footer right-aligned: at most one solid primary (the kit's btn, 30, radius 6) and quiet links. Esc and a click outside close (assumed for Herdr dialogs; if a click outside does not close, Cancel comes back as a quiet link).
Kansō The "Esc" printed in each corner goes: Esc always closes.

Seijaku One spacing everywhere: 24 inside every dialog, window and the Settings dialog, on all four sides (K); panels keep 16; only the kit's gaps between parts. No dialog has a fixed height: it ends 24 under its last line, so no empty band at the bottom. Settings scrolls only past 680.
Kansō A focused field wears the kit's focus ring, the only colour a dialog adds. Armed is the kit's: "Press again to …", accent, 4 s.

Shizen First read: the kit skeleton, breathing. Pending: marked at once on its row (the kit's pending, S21: 80% and the breathing dot), nothing else changes until it is done. Failure: the source's own words in blocked (two lines at most, the full text in the tooltip), then one action row: the retry (Refresh for a read, the action's own name for a write), then Explain to <agent>. Empty: one dim sentence, one action at most. The same classes on every board (pax-fail, pax-empty, pax-skl, pax-ck pend).
Seijaku Rename: "Empty: the name the program gives it" becomes the placeholder itself (claude): an emptied field shows what it falls back to.
Kansō kanso-prompt-editor is removed. Nothing in kansō opens it, and it printed its title twice (as title and label). The Pin note is the same kanso-prompt with lines: 4.
Kokō Remote: none. The answer is one hc label (on the terminal's computer) or one shared write.

Kansō Sleep this agent or tab is one press, with no dialog: the moon on the focused finished pane, or the tab's menu. The tab leaves at once, a toast offers Undo for 8 s, and the row goes into Asleep breathing.

Shizen Sleep a project opens a dialog only when something will not come back as it was, and says only that: "vite on web starts fresh on Wake". The tabs that keep their conversation are not listed; that is the default. When everything keeps its conversation, it sleeps at once like a tab. The primary counts: Sleep 3 tabs. Another computer is named in the title.
Kokō A blocker is the row's own fact ("working" with its mark) and one blocked line. No disabled button. The dialog already re-reads every 3 s; when the agent stops, it sleeps.

Kansō The Asleep dialog is removed. The sidebar's Asleep group was its second home. Every state lives on the group's rows: Going to sleep and Waking (pending: the moon breathes, the word is dim), stuck (the kit failure on the row: the step's own words, then Undo, the one action that fixes it; no Explain, no agent can act on it), asleep (Wake visible, Enter wakes), and unreachable (dimmed, no Wake). Wake all and Forget are in the row's menu.

Kansō One sentence per stuck step, from sleepwork.js: "cart-ui did not exit", "cart-ui's prompt could not be cleared", "cart-ui's conversation was not found". The toast, one line tall, uses the LINE size: the same words in blocked and the same action word (Undo), no Explain; only when the group is off screen.
Kokō Folded group: the count, plus "· 1 stuck" in blocked when one is. Open, no count: the rows are the count.
Kansō Forget and Wake all go to the row's menu. Forget is Armed with accent, not red text.
Kansō Every caption goes: "Every tab's agents exit and the tabs close…", "Put a tab you are waiting on to sleep…", "keeps its conversation" on every row.
Kokō Remote: the dialog reads one session file per agent on that computer, once, then every 3 s only while blocked. Removing the Asleep dialog removes its read of every computer's store on open.
Seijaku One shell (D1). One list, one line per arrangement, no icon (every row had the same one). A row from another project says that project at the right. Its panes are in the row's tooltip.
Kansō Overwrite and Delete show on the selected row, by state, instead of on every row. Enter opens. Delete is the kit's Armed in accent, not red text.
Kansō Save shows the tab's shape (columns at their widths, each pane's program and command) instead of a text list. An agent says "new conversation": that is the fact the teaching note carried.
Kansō Overwrite is not a second view. Typing a name already used turns the primary into "Overwrite web and api", which takes a second press.

Shizen Opening is marked at once on its row (the kit's pending, S21: 80% and the breathing dot) and the tab appears; nothing else changes until it is done. A refused delete puts git's or sqlite's words under that row, then Delete and Explain to checkout.
Kansō Empty: "No arrangement" and the primary. The three-line caption goes.
Kokō Remote: none to read; arrangements are in the local store. Opening on another computer starts each pane there (one hc call per pane).
Seijaku One shell. No scope line: the draft says where the work comes from. The "To" and "Message" labels go; the field and the box say it. Find shows once more than six agents run.
Kansō Each row is the agent's name, its project as one dim word, and its ensō mark. No program icon, no branch (the branch shows on the row under the pointer), no project heads.
Shizen An agent that needs you cannot take a message, so it is not offered; its home is the sidebar. "Sent. cart-ui waited on its own question and got nothing." can no longer happen.
Seijaku A press on a row's project word selects every agent there that can take it. The primary names the target: Send to tests, Send to 2 in acme-shop.
Kansō "Pasted into its terminal and sent with Enter, as if you typed it there." goes: a caption. Cancel goes: Esc closes.
Kokō Another computer: the dim word says it ("relay · devbox"). Unreachable: the row dims, says so, and is not a target.

Shizen Sending is marked at once on the target's row (the kit's pending, S21: 80% and the breathing dot); the dialog closes when hc confirms. Refused: hc's words under that row and nothing else: the terminal is gone, so no retry fixes it and no agent can act; the draft stays for another target.
Kansō A primary that cannot act is not drawn: with no target or an empty message there is no Send,.
Kokō Remote: no reads. One hc send per target, on that agent's computer.

Seijaku Popup on the one skeleton: title 15 semibold, the path as the scope line (the computer first when it is not this one), rows 32, the editor's name and nothing else. Number keys 1 to 9 show once the keyboard moves in the list.

Kansō The hints go: "last used" (it is already first), "split" (the row under the pointer says "in a split" for a terminal editor) and "no editor" (Preview is named Preview). The "In a split" heading goes. An editor that cannot open on another computer is not drawn there, so there is no "local only".
Kansō The 1px rule under the header and the "Esc" corner go.
Kansō The coloured letter tiles with white letters (six hex colours) go: the name tells the editors apart.
Seijaku Looking: the kit skeleton. None: one dim sentence. Failure: the probe's own words, then Refresh; no Explain (nothing an agent can do about mdfind).
Kokō Remote: none. Editors are found on this computer once and cached in open-with.found; on another computer the editor opens over its own SSH.

Kansō The window takes the panel skeleton (board 08): header 40, title 20 (the window is 560), ‹ only when a file is open, Close last. Source and Refresh show while the pointer is over the header. The bar under the header goes.

Yūgen The scope line carries the folder, and the save state only while it matters ("Saving…", "Edited"; saved is the rest state and is not said), or the stale line, or "612 KB, read only". Before, the save state was a fourth item in the header.
Yūgen Review: the scope line names who waits ("cart-ui waits for your review"), and Done is the one solid primary, in place of a bordered chip with a tooltip.

Kansō Telling md-review fails: the kit failure under the scope, md-review's own words, then Done (the write's own name) and Explain to cart-ui. The header's Done is not drawn while the failure shows, so there is one Done.
Yūgen "Read again" and "Retry" become Refresh. The tooltip says when it was read.

Kansō Changed on disk while you edit is drawn as P03's editor conflict: one line "Changed on disk at 14:06", then Overwrite and Reload, one press each; after Overwrite the line says "Saved over the 14:06 text" with Undo.
Kansō List: Waiting for your review, From this terminal, In this folder, as panel sections without counts; rows 32. Empty: "No Markdown in ~/infra". The Cmd-click tip goes.
Yūgen Blocks keep their hover (a double-click edits). An editing block is the raised slab with the kit's focus ring. A table edits as its grid.
Seijaku Same document as Preview in the side panel: one MarkdownDoc, two places. The words match Preview's.
Kokō Remote: one stat every 10 s while the window shows, and a full read only when size or mtime changes. Nothing while hidden. The list is read once, on open.

Yūgen Subtracted, measured on every dialog's first screen: rows 136 → 64, icons and marks 86 → 11, colours other than ink 10 → 4, pieces of text 245 → 106. No fact lost: the table says where each one appears when it matters.

Kansō Rule: at rest a dialog shows what you came for and what you would miss; the rest appears on the row under the pointer or the keyboard, when it changed, or when it needs you. States that need you (failure, armed, blocked) stay as loud as on D1 to D14.
Kokō Colour only on what asks: the solid primary, the accent of a focused field, an agent's ensō, the working colour on what will not come back. Everything else is ink or dim.

Kansō kansō settings loses its header link to Herdr settings: the footer's Settings menu is the one door to both (D12). Keys folds its list into eight group lines under the keyboard. What's new drops the version line (the you-are-here node says it) and Refresh (it reads on open).

Kokō Sleep a project says only what will not come back. Send lists only the agents that can take the text, with the project as a dim word on the row. Arrangements, Open with and Credits lose icons that did not tell rows apart.
Seijaku These first screens are now the first screens on D2 to D10, D13 and D14, and those boards' states speak the same rows. The old first screens live only here, as before.

Yūgen The board is the hero: 18 × 8 cells of 34, centred, as wide as the dialog allows. The cursor is the solid cell. The target is unmistakable: an accent ring, an accent wash and a dot. The best path appears only after a miss, as a trail with its first key on it ("l"), the hint the game already computes after 2 s (main.js:187).
Kansō Round progress is the board's top edge: ten segments, the current one half lit. The 6 px bar and "2 / 10" under the board go.

Kansō One quiet line above the board: score, time, streak, then the live count against the best, "2 moves · this one takes 5 at best". Over the best, the count turns working. The four stats in a grid go.

Kansō Hachi speaks: the line is Hachi's, beside Hachi, in a bubble on raised. Hachi's face follows the mood (calm, glad, sweat, sleep; mascot.js:28-36, unchanged), and the bubble's edge takes the mood's colour (glad in done, sweat in working). The floating name and the grey box far away go. Hachi's art, its 16 × 15 grid and its fur and cream are the code's own.

Yūgen The keys are the real keyboard under the board, four rows staggered as on a keyboard. The level's keys are raised; the rest are ghosts. The finger names appear once, under h j k l on the home row. The pressed key lights (solid); the hinted key takes the accent ring.

Seijaku The levels are a path: a done level is a filled done node with its best; the current one is ringed and washed; one not tried yet is hollow. [ and ] move along it and p opens the pet chooser, outside a round. The game locks no level, and neither does the path.
Kansō Keys only. A move starts a round, Enter plays again, n goes to the next level, Esc twice leaves. End round stays in the header for the mouse.

Seijaku The result takes the board's place, the same frame: the score at 48, "a new best for level 3 · was 120" in done, one quiet line of the rest (targets, fewest, streak, time), then the keys that act: ↩ play again, n next level.
Seijaku Level cleared: the path's node fills with its best and the next level is current, its tip in Hachi's words.
Seijaku All nine done: the path is full, the total across it, and Hachi glad.
Seijaku Share is the one menu of Q7 from the header icon, "Scores and practice days only", shown once a round is played.
Kansō Esc once: Hachi's bubble turns accent, "Press Esc again to leave the dōjō" (3 s, code's ARM_MS). The header stays as it is: one place says it. A round ended early: "Round stopped, not counted."
Seijaku Asleep after 20 s with no round: Hachi's sleep face and "z z".
Seijaku The same screens on the light tokens. Hachi keeps its fur and cream in both themes; its outline, eyes and nose take chrome, its tongue accent, its drop of sweat blue, as mascot.js:39-41.
Kokō Fix: in light, chrome is pale, so Hachi's outline and eyes vanish on the light card. Outline, eyes and nose take the art's own dark ink, #161615 (mascot.js's fallback), in light.
